proposals.title: Muse Code one-off runs, models, and images
proposals.prompt:
Everything else Suspense does with a harness also works with Muse
Code. A one-off run uses Muse Code in a mode that can only read,
glob, and search, never change anything, as
spec/scope/harness-integration/one-off-run/index.pi#OneOffAgentRun
says. The chat input's model picker lists the models Muse Code can
be told, and the effort picker is enabled only if Muse Code takes a
reasoning effort, as spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi#ChatInput
describes for the others. Attached images go to Muse Code the way it
takes them, as
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.images
says. Muse Code's skills, commands, and agents appear in
spec/scope/harness-integration/catalog/index.pi#HarnessCatalog if it
reports them. If Muse Code has no way to do one of these, the spec
says so.

spec.note: Muse Code's read-only mode for one-off runs
spec.quote: Claude Code is given only those tools, Codex runs in its read-only sandbox, and OpenCode runs as its plan agent

spec.note: the model and effort pickers for Muse Code
spec.quote: for Codex and OpenCode, the models their own configuration lists

spec.note: how attached images are given to Muse Code
spec.quote: Images attached to a prompt ... are given to the harness as it takes them

spec.note: Muse Code's skills, commands, and agents
spec.quote: Every harness run reports the skills and agents it has

proposals.title: Run tasks with Muse Code
proposals.prompt:
Muse Code can be the harness a project's runs go to, alongside Claude Code,
Codex, and OpenCode. The spec has nothing on Muse Code yet, so this is new:
work out its real command, flags, streamed JSON events, system-prompt
support, conversation resume and fork, image arguments, and where it keeps
its sessions and its directory from Muse Code's own documentation and
`--help`. Never guess them; where something can't be found, say so.

Add Muse Code to spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.harnesses
with how it is run, and read its events into the same reply, tool calls,
usage, and result as the others. Cover what
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.feeding,
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.images,
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.context, and
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.failures say for
each harness. If it takes no system prompt of its own, give the system prompt
ahead of the prompt the way Codex and OpenCode do. Name its directory for
HARNESS_DIRECTORY in spec/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.pi#ModeSystemPrompts.
Find its command as spec/scope/application/index.pi#Application.findingPrograms
says, and offer it as a row in spec/scope/settings-window/index.pi#SettingsWindow.agent,
with its command muted beside it and "Not installed" when that command can't
be found. Every run kind (tasks, questions, palette search, one-off runs,
notes, commit messages, titles) works with it, under its mode's sandbox, the
same as with any other harness.

spec.note: the list of harnesses and how each is run, which Muse Code joins
spec.quote: The harness in use is the project's: Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode

spec.note: the one-off commands it names
spec.quote: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`, whichever the user chose

spec.note: whether Muse Code can be fed more while it works
spec.quote: read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work

spec.note: how images are passed to each harness
spec.quote: are given to the harness as it takes them

spec.note: where its sessions are kept, copied and restored
spec.quote: Codex and OpenCode sessions are kept and restored the same way, wherever each harness keeps them

spec.note: its errors shown in its own words
spec.quote: in the harness's own words

spec.note: a row for Muse Code in the harness picker
spec.quote: a row for each harness, in order: Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode

spec.note: finding Muse Code's command on the host
spec.quote: each harness, Claude Code's `claude`, Codex's `codex`, and OpenCode's `opencode`

spec.note: what HARNESS_DIRECTORY is for Muse Code
spec.quote: HARNESS_DIRECTORY is the directory the harness that runs the prompt

spec.note: Muse Code itself (its command, flags, JSON event stream, session store or directory); searched the whole compiled reference for
spec.quote: muse

proposals.title: Settle the Muse Code harness in the spec
proposals.prompt:
Settle spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.harnesses,
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.feeding,
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.images, and
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.context with what
the code now does for Muse Code: the exact command and flags, whether it can
be fed or fork a conversation, how it takes images, where its sessions live,
and which small model, if any, writes the notes, commit messages, and titles.

spec.note: Muse Code's command and flags as built
spec.quote: Each harness is run its own way

spec.note: where Muse Code's sessions are kept, as built
spec.quote: wherever each harness keeps them

proposals.title: Check Muse Code on the welcome page
proposals.prompt:
With Muse Code as the project's harness, the "Harness" and "Harness login"
rows of spec/scope/welcome/index.pi#Welcome.checks speak of Muse Code. They
find it with its version command, link to its installation instructions when
it's missing, report whether it is logged in using its own status command,
and name its login command with "Open terminal" when it isn't. The spec has
nothing on Muse Code yet, so this is new. Take its URL and commands from Muse
Code's own documentation, never invent them.

spec.note: the Harness and Harness login rows for Muse Code, "links to the harness's installation instructions" and
spec.quote: as its own status command reports

spec.note: Muse Code's install page, version command, or login status and login commands

proposals.title: Model and effort pickers for Muse Code
proposals.prompt:
With Muse Code in use, the model picker in
spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi#ChatInput.tabs.model lists the
models Muse Code can be told and passes the chosen one in the way Muse Code
takes it. The effort picker in
spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi#ChatInput.tabs.effort offers its
levels if Muse Code takes a reasoning effort, and is disabled otherwise, as
for Claude Code and OpenCode. Both are remembered per harness, as
spec/scope/user-preferences/index.pi#UserPreferences.preferences says. The
spec has nothing on Muse Code's models or efforts yet, so this is new. Take
them from Muse Code's own documentation.

spec.note: the models listed for each harness
spec.quote: The models listed are those the harness can be told

spec.note: which harnesses offer an effort
spec.quote: Only a harness that takes a reasoning effort offers it

spec.note: the choice remembered for each harness
spec.quote: remembered for the user, per harness

spec.note: which models and reasoning efforts Muse Code accepts, and how it is told them

proposals.title: Offer Muse Code when creating or importing a project
proposals.prompt:
Muse Code can be picked as a new or imported project's harness, as
spec/scope/new-project/index.pi#NewProject.agents and
spec/scope/import-project/index.pi#ImportProject.defaults describe for the
others. A project with no harness saved defaults to Muse Code when its
piton.config.pi builds only for Muse Code's adapter, as
spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi#HarnessIntegration.harnesses says.
The Agents group lists only agents Belay has an adapter for, and the spec
names no Muse Code adapter. First check whether @piton/belay has one. If it
doesn't, stop and say so rather than inventing one, because the rest of this
story depends on it.

spec.note: the Agents checkboxes and the Harness radio group
spec.quote: one per agent Belay has an adapter for

spec.note: the harness an imported project starts with
spec.quote: The template, the agents, and the harness start as a new project's do

spec.note: the default harness from piton.config.pi's adapters
spec.quote: by its adapters in order, Claude Code for ClaudeCodeAdapter

spec.note: a Belay adapter for Muse Code
